nodes.label: Handyman Skill Definition
nodes.rationale: v1.5.0 compresses SKILL.md into a compact always-loaded core and delegates detail to references/ so it stays within the 1000-word body and 500-char description token budgets.

nodes.label: Handyman Operating Modes
nodes.rationale: Five explicit modes (analyze, bootstrap, run-feature, review, migrate-global) keep each invocation scoped; when unclear, start with analyze.

nodes.label: Installation Scope (Local vs Global)
nodes.rationale: local versions the harness next to the code under PROJECT_ROOT/.handyman keeping the repo root clean; global keeps operational history out of the source tree under $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project_name>.

nodes.label: Handyman Core Rules
nodes.rationale: Hard operating constraints (disk as source of truth, verifier-gated closure, role separation) exist so agent work stays auditable and resumable instead of living only in chat.

nodes.label: One Feature At A Time Rule
nodes.rationale: Working a single lowest-id pending feature limits context mixing and accidental cross-feature changes, and makes interrupted sessions resumable from disk state.

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered fallback (harness.config.json, then feature_list.json config, then PROJECT_ROOT/.handyman, then legacy PROJECT_ROOT) keeps new local/global installs deterministic while legacy harnesses keep working.

nodes.label: Anti-Telefono-Descompuesto Pattern
nodes.rationale: Long reports persist as backlog/ files (impl_, review_, explore_) and the chat carries only short references like 'done -> backlog/impl_cli_edit.md', preventing information degradation when work passes between agents.

nodes.label: Graphify Context Layer
nodes.rationale: The knowledge graph is queried before exploring code and kept fresh via the post-commit hook or /graphify --update, so agents reuse indexed context instead of re-reading the repo.

nodes.label: Per-Role Model Assignment
nodes.rationale: Strong reasoning model only for the leader; implementer and reviewer use cheap fast models (editor-configured, fallback Claude Sonnet 4.6) to control cost without hurting coordination quality.

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Tools Per Role
nodes.rationale: Each role gets only the capabilities it needs: leader widest (agent, web, browser); implementer and reviewer without delegation or web; explorer read-only with no edit.

nodes.label: Leader Role
nodes.rationale: Coordinates the harness and delegates; never edits product code.

nodes.label: Implementer Role
nodes.rationale: Implements exactly one feature with tests and leaves evidence on disk.

nodes.label: Reviewer Role
nodes.rationale: Validates against architecture, conventions, checkpoints and the verifier; never edits code; returns only APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED plus a file reference.

nodes.label: Explorer Role
nodes.rationale: Cheapest model, read-only tool surface (no edit, no agent); used for reconnaissance reports under backlog/explore_<topic>.md.

nodes.label: Obsidian Vault Integration
nodes.rationale: HARNESS_WORKSPACE doubles as an Obsidian vault (YAML frontmatter in reports, index.md MOC, #handyman/... tags) so harness state is browsable without duplicating files; .obsidian/ and .trash/ stay gitignored as local metadata.

nodes.label: Deterministic Scaffolding (scaffold.sh)
nodes.rationale: scripts/scaffold.sh <local|global> <project_root> copies templates without ever overwriting, making bootstrap reproducible; agents then fill the copied templates with project-specific content.

nodes.label: Foreman (harness-subagents) Predecessor
nodes.rationale: Handyman supersedes Foreman/harness-subagents, adding install scopes, per-role models and tools, backlog reports and Obsidian integration; prefer Handyman when both could match.
